baseline.methods: HMI calculates a pooled distribution of subgroup medians across the admitted sampling families. Each family has equal total weight, then each country, township or rice category within that family has equal weight. This estimates the position of a typical source subgroup, not the median of every individual rice sample worldwide. Raw measurements first supply subgroup medians; published subgroup medians remain summary units. Study means, maxima and ranges are never inserted as individual samples. The rating evaluates the row’s displayed source mean or median against the pooled subgroup-median distribution; a mean is not relabelled as a median, and skewed distributions can give different positions for these statistics. The same frozen reference is used for every eligible finding and does not change with filters. baseline.methods: HMI calculates a pooled distribution of subgroup medians across the admitted sampling families. Each family has equal total weight, then each country, township or rice category within that family has equal weight. This estimates the position of a typical source subgroup, not the median of every individual rice sample worldwide. Raw measurements first supply subgroup medians; published subgroup medians remain summary units. Study means, maxima and ranges are never inserted as individual samples. The rating evaluates the row’s displayed source mean or median against the pooled subgroup-median distribution; a mean is not relabelled as a median, and skewed distributions can give different positions for these statistics. The same frozen reference is used for every eligible finding and does not change with filters. Myanmar dry-weight observations are converted to original grain mass with the study’s measured 6–7% moisture loss (×0.93–0.94); Saudi ground-grain measurements retain their analysed mass. No generic moisture assumption is applied. These ordinary farm/market sampling frames form a historical international occurrence reference. Saudi subgroups retain reported origin; triplicate laboratory analyses count once per rice sample. Song’s fresh-weight mean and Tran’s air-dried genotype estimates are external comparisons at native grain moisture; they do not set the reference. Residual moisture and experimental field selection limit those comparisons. Yan’s censored median is 0–LOD, not its published half-LOD point.
baseline.limitations: The collection is historical and geographically uneven, with small numbers of sampling families. Country, township and category subgroups have different sampling frames. It is an evidence-library reference, not a probability sample of the world market. Source analytical and rounding uncertainty remains; censoring bounds are not confidence intervals. The selected finding can contribute to its reference. Low / Moderate / High describes concentration position, not health risk, compliance, certainty or a causal rice-form effect.
